subject: Transit hops & processing site inventory request
messages:
From: Amit Desai <amit@syncwave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@syncwave.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Transit hops & processing site inventory request

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — SyncWave liked the latency profile but Legal needs a detailed map of where inference requests actually travel and which vendors touch data. Can you provide:

- A per-region inventory of compute locations you execute inference in (hosted + any common cloud partners).
- A list of subprocessors that process/transit request payloads (compute, caching, CDN, logs).
- Clarify what is kept transiently vs persisted (KV cache, prefix cache, logs), and the retention windows.
- Evidence we can hand to our InfoSec: example trace for a request from London -> your hosted API showing hops, timestamps, and which subprocessor saw the payload.
- Whether you perform any cross-border caching (CDN or redis outside EU) by default, and options to constrain to EU-only.

We have a SOC2 review next Friday so any quick artifacts (roster CSV, architecture map) would be helpful.

Thanks,
Amit
Head of Platform
SyncWave Health

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@syncwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transit hops & processing site inventory request

Hi Amit — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise inventory and I attached a high-level hop map and our current subprocessor roster. I can also schedule a 30-min run-through with Marissa (our compliance lead) if that helps.

Summary (hosted/default):
- Primary execution regions (we run inference close to the caller by default):
  * europe-west-1 (AWS - Ireland) — primary for EU queries
  * eu-central-1 (AWS - Frankfurt) — failover/low-latency for DACH customers
  * us-east-1 (AWS - N. Virginia) and us-west1 (GCP - us-west1) for NA traffic
  * asia-southeast1 (GCP - Singapore) for APAC

- Subprocessors (short list; full roster attached):
  * CloudSpan Computing (GCP) — managed compute pools for some model variants
  * EdgeNet CDN — optional streaming/edge caching for large multimodal payloads
  * KeyVaultCo — KMS for customer key wrapping (when KMS integrated)
  * LogFlow Systems — audit log retention and search (default retention 30 days)
  * MetricsHub — aggregated telemetry (anonymized metrics only)

- What is transient vs persisted:
  * In-memory KV cache (GPU node RAM) — ephemeral, never written to disk, TTL typically seconds–minutes.
  * Prefix cache (optional Redis) — if enabled on Hosted, runs in-region by default; for some customers we run Redis clusters managed by CloudSpan and those can be pinned to region (EU-only) via contract. Persisted only for configured TTLs (default 1 hour).
  * Request logs / diagnostic traces — kept in LogFlow for 30 days by default; can be configured to shorter windows or routed to customer-owned storage for enterprise plans.

- Cross-border caching:
  * Default behavior: routing is latency-first within policy boundaries; EU-origin traffic is routed to our EU pools unless the customer has opted into global routing or model variants not available in-region.
  * EdgeNet (CDN) may cache streamed blobs at the edge for up to 1 hour unless explicitly disabled. We can enforce EU-only caching for SyncWave by enabling EU-edge policy or by using a Dedicated/Private deployment.

- Deletion and evidence:
  * Deletion API: /v1/enterprise/requests/{id}/erase — immediate soft-delete + async purge from persistent stores within 24–72 hours depending on store.
  * KV/prefix caches: TTL-based eviction; on explicit erase we invalidate keys and notify Redis clusters; in-memory caches drop on process restart — no durable copy.
  * Audit evidence: we can produce a redacted trace showing timestamps, region, and subprocessors involved for a sample request. Full request payloads are not included in evidence unless customer provides consent.

Attachments: processing_hop_map.pdf (hop diagram), subprocessor_roster.csv (current roster), redwood_data_retention_summary.pdf (retention defaults + enterprise options).

If you want a deeper packet-level trace, Marissa can pull our trace for a London-origin request and provide the anonymized timeline. Interested in a quick call later today?

Cheers,
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Amit Desai <amit@syncwave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal <legal@syncwave.ai>
Date: 2026-10-28T13:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transit hops & processing site inventory request

Jordan — that was helpful, thanks. A couple of follow-ups from Legal/Infra: 

1) Can you confirm whether EdgeNet ever writes cached content to persistent object storage outside EU for more than 24 hours (they're particularly concerned about audio blobs).
2) For the LogFlow logs: can you produce an audit CSV showing which internal subprocessor account accessed the log for a sample trace (we need to show chain of custody)?
3) Export control question — do any subprocessors or cloud partners route through non-EEA jurisdictions for control or compliance reasons (e.g., routing through US KMS endpoints)?

If SyncWave can get explicit confirmation for 1–3 and a redacted trace, we can close the SOC2 evidence request.

Thanks,
Amit

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amit Desai <amit@syncwave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-29T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Transit hops & processing site inventory request

Amit — quick answers inline, plus next steps:

1) EdgeNet persistence: EdgeNet may temporarily store streamed artifacts at edge POPs up to 1 hour by default; they do not write to persistent object storage outside the region unless configured to do so (we do not enable cross-region object spill for EU customers). We will provide a dated statement from EdgeNet in the evidence pack. If you need zero-edge-persistence, we can: a) disable edge caching for your account, or b) run traffic through an EU-only edge pool (Dedicated/Private).

2) LogFlow chain-of-custody: Yes — LogFlow records access events and we can export an audit CSV that includes internal service-account identifiers, timestamps, and the role that accessed the trace. We will provide a redacted sample that shows which internal account performed the retrieval (no payload contents).

3) Export controls / KMS: By default, our Hosted control plane may use globally-available control plane endpoints for orchestration, but customer data encryption keys (when customers use our KMS integration) are pinned to regional KMS endpoints per contract. For SyncWave, if you require EU-key residency we can:
  * Use customer-managed keys in an EU KMS (recommended), or
  * Enable our EU-only KMS pool (contract addendum).

Next steps:
- I attached the quick evidence pack (processing_hop_map.pdf + subprocessor_roster.csv).
- Marissa will pull an anonymized trace (London-origin) and sanitized LogFlow access CSV by EOD and upload to the Drive folder linked below.
- If helpful, we can follow up with a short legal-to-legal Q&A and provide a signed statement from EdgeNet and CloudSpan about regional processing guarantees.

Let me know if you'd like the Dedicated trial for EU-only enforcement; we can spin up a trial tenant and pin compute and caches to eu-west-1 exclusively.

Best,
Jordan

P.S. Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B3cREDWOOD-syncwave-evidence
